_comment: Which model tier each component runs on, in one place.
Components must never name a concrete model version (claude-haiku-4-5-...).
Aliases already track the newest model of their family - the docs are explicit:
'Aliases point to the recommended version for your provider and update over
time. To pin to a specific version, use the full model name.' So version drift
is the platform's job, not ours.
What this file adds on top is the SEMANTIC layer the platform has no concept
of: which KIND of work a component does. Claude Code's frontmatter only speaks
families (haiku/sonnet/opus), and it performs no variable substitution in the
`model:` field - only in skill body text and allowed-tools - so the mapping
cannot happen at runtime. It happens here, at build time, applied by
Re-tiering a role (say Haiku grows capable enough to own `build`) is a
one-line edit here followed by `python scripts/gen-models.py`. Deciding
WHETHER to re-tier is a judgement call and stays a human's: the criteria
below are the test, not the frequency of the task.

chore.criterion: Needs no judgement on any given run. Locating files, running a known command, executing a stated git operation, mechanical rewrites.

build.criterion: Engineering judgement inside a fixed contract. Writing code to a spec, reviewing one diff through one lens, recovering decisions already made.

think.criterion: Design trade-offs and repair. Architecture choices, reviewing a plan against its requirements, ambiguous requirements.
